hints: Count the horizontal divisions for one complete sine wave on each CRO screen, from the same point on the wave to the next identical point.
Multiply your divisions-per-cycle by the stated time-base setting in $\text{s/div}$ to get the period $T$ in seconds for each screen.
Use $f = 1/T$ and look for the two screens where the larger divisions-per-cycle is balanced by the smaller time-base setting to give equal $T$.
walkthrough: Count divisions for one period: screen 1 shows about 4 horizontal divisions per cycle and screen 2 shows about 2 horizontal divisions per cycle.
State the rule $T = \text{divisions per cycle} \times \text{time-base}$ and $f = 1/T$, so equal $f$ means equal $T$.
For 2: $T_2 \approx 2 \times 0.04\text{ s} = 0.08\text{ s}$, so $f_2 \approx 12.5\text{ Hz}$, identical to screen 1.
Check the others: $T_3 \approx 2 \times 0.01\text{ s} = 0.02\text{ s}$ and $T_4 \approx 4 \times 0.08\text{ s} = 0.32\text{ s}$, neither equals $0.08\text{ s}$.
Therefore screens 1 and 2 have the same frequency. This is option A.
